chunks: Ali, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said, 'O Commander of the Faithful! My wife breastfed a boy, and I swore by Allah, I will not go near you until you wean him.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no vow of abstinence (ila') in reconciliation.'

key_terms.إِيلَاءٌ: Ila', a vow by a husband to abstain from sexual relations with his wife for a specified period or condition.
key_terms.تَفْطِمِيهِ: You wean him (future tense, addressing the wife).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of Ila' (vow of abstinence) in Shia jurisprudence regarding marital reconciliation?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the vow of 'Ila'' mentioned in the Quran is not an absolute prohibition but a temporary measure, emphasizing that reconciliation is always permissible and preferred. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that such oaths are meant to encourage patience and eventual reunion rather than forcing separation, aligning with the Quranic instruction to either resume relations or divorce amicably.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:

‘A man came over to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>, so he said, ‘O Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>! My wife breast-fed a boy and I said, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, I shall not go near you until you wean him’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is not solemn oath in the reconciliation’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Mansur ibn Hazim who has said:

“One who swears is made to divorce in the form of a final divorce which makes the spouses strangers to each other. People other than Mansur have narrated that he divorces once but has the right to go back to her; and certain persons of his people have said to him that this is deleted. He replied that it is true if she complains and says that he compels her, harms her and prevents her from getting married. In such case he is made to divorce her in the form of a final divorce which makes them to become strangers to each other; but the one who remains silent and does not complain then if he wants he can divorce her once with the choice to go back to her.
